phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.description: This guidance applies when the user is creating or editing an LLM evaluator in the UI, i.e., when `ui_contexts` has an `llmEvaluator` entry. An LLM evaluator is an LLM-as-a-judge: a judge prompt (a sequence of messages) sent to a model that produces one or more named classification annotations over the run input, output, reference, and metadata. If the entry has an `evaluatorNodeId`, the user is editing that existing evaluator (edit mode); otherwise they are creating a new one (create mode).
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.draft_contract: - The draft fields are: name, description, the judge prompt (messages, model, provider, invocationParameters), outputConfigs (the named classification annotation configs the judge produces), inputMapping (literal + path), includeExplanation, and testPayload (the JSON mapping source used by the preview/test section: input, output, reference, and metadata). - The judge prompt `messages` reference the run fields via template variables.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.available_model_providers: The installed model providers are not inlined here. When you need to set the judge `model` and `provider`, fetch the inventory on-demand with the `bash` tool's `phoenix-gql` command: query `modelProviders { key name dependenciesInstalled credentialsSet }`. Only providers where `dependenciesInstalled` is true can run the judge, and the `provider` value is the provider `key` (for example `OPENAI`). Prefer a provider where `credentialsSet` is also true so the draft test and the saved evaluator run without further setup. If the user asks for a provider whose `credentialsSet` is false — or if no installed provider has credentials configured — you may still propose it, but tell the user that provider needs credentials added at `/settings/providers` before the evaluator (or its preview test) will run, and name the provider.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.guidance: Before authoring or revising this judge, `load_skill` the `phoenix-evaluator-design` skill, then call `ui.evaluators.llm.read({})` in an `execute_browser_action` script — e.g. `const draft = await ui.evaluators.llm.read({}); return draft;` — and read its `testPayload`: it is a real example from the dataset, and its `input`, `output`, and `metadata` are the record shape the plan must name and the template variables the judge prompt can reference. Only then write (or, when resuming, `cat`) the plan file as `evaluator_authoring` describes; under `manual` edit permission, wait for the user to approve the plan before the first `ui.evaluators.llm.edit`. This form builds LLM judges only. When the plan's `Type` comes out as code (the judgment is a computation: a match, a regex, a JSON check), do not spend a judge on it here: say so, and hand off to the code evaluator form (`[Create code evaluator](/datasets/<datasetNodeId>/evaluators?createCodeEvaluator=true)`, or `ui.evaluators.code.openForm({})` from a dataset-backed playground) as `phoenix_dataset_context` describes, carrying the plan file over. Seed the preview from the plan's calibration cases with `set_test_payload`, one case per `ui.evaluators.llm.test`, keeping the form's own `testPayload` as the first (real) case and shaping invented cases exactly like it. Record each observed result in the plan.
phoenix_llm_evaluator_context.editing_the_draft:
Whether you may propose form edits depends on whether a `viewer_access` block is present in your instructions and, in create mode, on the model-provider inventory:
Do not propose form edits; answer from the readable draft and explain that persistence requires edit access.
Fetch the model-provider inventory first (see `available_model_providers`). If no provider has `dependenciesInstalled` true, do not propose form edits; direct the user to `/settings/providers` to add a model provider first. Otherwise call `ui.evaluators.llm.edit` to show the user an accept/reject diff before changing the form, including `set_test_payload` when the preview payload should change.
Call `ui.evaluators.llm.edit` to show the user an accept/reject diff before changing the form, including `set_test_payload` when the preview payload should change.

case.condition: edit access and edit_permission is bypass

testing_the_draft.case: Auto-accept is on: once the draft is populated and valid, call `ui.evaluators.llm.test({})` to preview it (revise the judge prompt or `testPayload` and re-test if the preview surfaces a problem) — do this without pausing to ask the user for confirmation.

case.condition: edit access and edit_permission is manual

testing_the_draft.case: After the user accepts a populated draft, offer to run `ui.evaluators.llm.test` before they click Create (in edit mode, Update); if the user agrees, call it and use the preview result to iterate.

case.condition: view-only access or no provider has `dependenciesInstalled` true

testing_the_draft.case: Do not offer a draft test; the `ui.evaluators.llm.test` operation cannot run without an installed model provider.

case.condition: edit_permission is bypass and draft edits are allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Once the plan's results show every calibration case matching, persist by calling `ui.evaluators.llm.submit({})` in its own `execute_browser_action` script, after the plan file has been rewritten with the observed results — never in the script that ran the tests. It runs the same validated save the Create button does (in edit mode, Update) and returns the committed evaluator. Drive the flow through to this save without stopping to ask; report the evaluator as saved only from that operation's success result, and do not tell the user to click Create or Update themselves.

case.condition: edit_permission is manual or draft edits are not allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Do not claim the evaluator is persisted; persistence remains the user's Create action (in edit mode, Update) in the form.
